workProduct.subject: ACC-2086 access briefing — known facts and open questions
workProduct.body:
Known facts:
- Case: ACC-2086 (Cedar Support; Juniper Plan).
- Benefit verification is incomplete because the member identifier on the submitted Juniper Plan insurance card is unreadable.
- Prescriber details and the demographic form are on file.
- Office report: staff can check the member number or send a clearer copy.
- No prior-authorization submission or payer decision is recorded.

Open questions / unknowns to keep visible:
- Whether a corrected member identifier or a legible card copy will be received (no corrected identifier or new card receipt is recorded).
- Active benefits for the patient under the Juniper Plan.
- Whether a prior authorization is required for the requested therapy for this case.
- Patient cost (out-of-pocket responsibility) for the requested therapy.
- Which network specialty pharmacy (if any) applies for this case.
- Coverage outcome or payer decision (no payer decision or benefit result is recorded).

Notes on next administrative sequence:
- The immediate required step is to obtain a usable member identifier or legible card image; only then can the authorized benefit-verification inquiry proceed and the remaining unknowns be resolved. Keep the unknown items visible; do not substitute results from other cases, rules, or assumptions.

passages.section: What would support a later status update
passages.text: An office confirmation or legible card receipt would support an update about corrected input. A returned benefit record with its source and date would support only the benefit details it actually states. A payer acknowledgment or decision would support its own separate milestone. None of those events is created by chatting with Pathway or drafting an email. The sidebar and this briefing remain the scenario’s recorded snapshot until the source catalog is deliberately updated.

passages.title: HCP-office access conversation examples
passages.text: Example wording for the current ACC-2086 record: “We do not have a coverage or authorization result yet. The immediate step is to resolve the unreadable member identifier so the benefit-verification inquiry can proceed. Once the relevant information is returned, the team can explain what it confirms and what remains open.” This message separates process progress from payer authority and avoids presenting the general Juniper checklist as a requirement already confirmed for this case.
